evidence: A silicon atomic layer was grown on a carbon-terminated c(2 × 2) sample surface at 1050 °C by exposure to Si2H6 at a partial pressure of 1 x 10^-6 Torr. A carbon atomic layer was grown at 1050 °C by exposure to C2H2 at a partial pressure of 1 x 10^-6 Torr on the silicon-covered (3 x 2) sample prepared by Si2H6 exposure. The purge time for each gas was about 5 min, including the LEED observation time, which reduces the pressure to around 1 x 10^-9 Torr.
